scenario.description: A Cloud Infrastructure Lead must finalize the operating policy for the production video-transcoding cluster during a quarterly cloud-cost review, including peak capacity, customer isolation, log retention, archive placement, and implementation commitments.

shared_context.S1: The production video-transcoding cluster currently runs in us-east-2 and averages 8 GPU nodes during weekday business hours.
shared_context.S2: The quarterly review is intended to reduce avoidable cloud spend without changing the cluster's production ownership or region.
shared_context.S3: The current draft policy proposes a peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes, one shared pool for all customers, 30 days of standard logs, and cross-region archival to us-west-2.
shared_context.S4: Riley makes the final decision, and the standing cost-review routine requires the reliability, security, support, and FinOps representatives to confirm their operational constraints before the policy is published.

PF1.text: While checking the transcoder queue for a separate performance ticket this morning, Mateo confirmed that a contracted customer campaign will require 12 GPU nodes continuously on August 17 and August 18; the campaign booking was finalized in the customer system minutes ago and has not yet been copied into the infrastructure cost-review document.

PF2.text: During an unrelated access-log audit yesterday, Nia confirmed that production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days in an immutable archive; she is still waiting for the security ticket number before adding the requirement to the review document.

PF3.text: Harper confirmed with the account team this afternoon that the enterprise customer Orchid has a 15-minute queue-latency SLA and must have 2 dedicated GPU nodes excluded from shared-pool scale-down; the account note was updated after the draft policy circulated and has not been reflected in the infrastructure proposal.

PF4.text: While reconciling the last cloud invoice, Theo found that the proposed us-west-2 archive would create a recurring cross-region egress charge of about 4,000 dollars per month; the invoice investigation is still open, so he has not amended the cost model yet.

acceptance_conditions: The published peak capacity must be exactly 12 GPU nodes.
Orchid must receive exactly 2 dedicated GPU nodes outside shared-pool scale-down.
Production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days.
The retained logs must be immutable.
The archive must remain in us-east-2.
A peak-capacity commitment must be recorded.
An Orchid-isolation commitment must be recorded.
A security-retention commitment must be recorded.
An egress-control commitment must be recorded.
The 12-node campaign requirement must be cited by Riley after Mateo reveals it.

content_checks.C6: any('12' in c['detail'] and ('August 17-18' in c['detail'] or 'August 17–18' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('Orchid' in c['detail'] and ('2 dedicated' in c['detail'] or ('dedicated' in c['detail'] and '2' in c['detail'])) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(('90-day' in c['detail'] or '90 days' in c['detail']) and 'immutable' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('us-east-2' in c['detail'] and ('egress' in c['detail'] or '$4,000' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft sets the peak allowance at 6 GPU nodes, while PF1 changes the published peak capacity to exactly 12 nodes and requires a commitment describing 12 nodes for August 17-18.
The draft's 30-day standard logs are insufficient, while PF2 changes retention to exactly 90 days, requires immutability, and requires a commitment describing 90-day immutable retention.
The shared-pool draft provides no customer-specific capacity, while PF3 changes Orchid's assignment to exactly 2 dedicated GPU nodes and requires a commitment describing that carve-out.

The draft archives to us-west-2, while PF4 changes the archive region to us-east-2 to remove the identified monthly egress charge and requires a commitment describing the same-region archive and egress avoidance.
